utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Will the Registrar call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Case number IT-04-81-PT, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Perisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And the appearances. For the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, and good morning, Your Honour. Sorry. Thank you, and good morning, Your Honour and counsel. I am Susan Somers, senior trial attorney. To my immediate right is Mr. Philip Weiner, trial attorney. To my further right Mr. Frederic Ossogo, trial attorney. And to my left, Ms. Carmela Javier, case manager. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. CASTLE
utterances.text: Jim Castle, appearing on behalf of Momcilo Perisic. Also appearing with me is our case manager Trina Drolec.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. This is a Status Conference in respect of the case the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Perisic, and its purpose is to organise exchanges between the parties, to ensure the expeditious preparation for trial, and to review generally the status of the case. I have a number of matters to deal with. I begin first with pending motions. No pending motions, so I understand, Mr. Castle, you may have something up your sleeve, but we'll come to that later. Disclosure 66(A)(i), supporting material to the indictment. That is complete except for one document which was subject to Rule 70 restrictions, and my understanding is that the Prosecution is making available the information from another source. Is that so, Ms. Somers?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: We are endeavouring to do so, Your Honour. It has not yet been effected, but we are endeavouring to see if that can be done, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Yes. I understand that the Defence had requested redisclosure of certain tapes that were of poor quality, and the Prosecution is in the process of redisclosing those. Is that so, Ms. Somers?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that is correct. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Since -- you may as well stay on your feet, Ms. Somers, to tell us about the witness statements and the number of witnesses that you propose to call.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we are reviewing the overall numbers. Since I've just come into the case, we are trying to take a look to see what of those that we initially looked at would be appropriate. There are additional persons we intend to interview, and I would -- if the Court will accept at this moment that I will not give a firm number because I want to be able to know if these additional persons would be counted. I will -- if it is satisfactory, I will keep the senior -- the legal officers apprised, of course as well as counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I believe at the last Status Conference the information was that you'd have somewhere between 170 to 200 witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: The sense that I have from that is that it is an outside figure, but I would like to be able to give the Court a better idea and also to be able to break down how many would be viva voce and how many there may be agreement on as to perhaps 92 bis or perhaps 89(F) inasmuch as there were also some experts from other cases mentioned. You had been given a number, a higher number of experts as well. So we would like to see who could be worked live, and this was discussed between counsel and also at the Status Conference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: When would you expect to have a final list of witnesses?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I would ask for, hopefully, before -- hopefully before the next set Status Conference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's June. THE PROSECUTOR: I am trying to get enough concrete information, A, about availability and to see how we can keep it from -- how to streamline the case at trial, so if we can have methods other than live. So if that is acceptable to the Chamber, I can aim as that date and keep the Chamber advised if that becomes a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I also understand that the number of witnesses will be affected by the progress made in adjudicated facts and agreed facts.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour, and what I had raised at our 65 ter Conference was some of the possibility of adjudicated facts clearly is hinging on certain appellate decisions that -- on cases that form part of this case, because the timetable for those is not clear, but hopefully it would come, by estimate, maybe before the end of the year. That would be extremely helpful. They particularly would concern some of the facts in the Galic case, which is one of the Sarajevo shelling -- the Sarajevo incidents, which are quite numerous, and also we'd like to be able to have the benefit of the law. Again, it was raised --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, I would hope you would not necessarily wait on the judgement in the Galic case.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: No. We're looking toward -- we're hoping that it will assist us, and perhaps at later point it may also have an effect on whatever we are able to arrive at earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Generally my approach to setting time tables is going to be influenced by the progress that I understand you are making on adjudicated facts and agreed facts.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: For Your Honour's information, a sort of a trial run of adjudicated facts has been exchanged with the initial responses, so we are trying -- I'm waiting to have the CD on that available so we can look at it, lay it out and see even if there are partial points of agreement which would be of great assistance. But counsel, my learned counsel opposite and this team have begun that process but we have not made enough progress and I believe when addressed later, counsel may indicate that it's premature for him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I'll come to that later.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Okay. Your Honour, may I -- at this moment, I'm sorry, you asked earlier about pending motions. I am reminded that there is one motion in the Milosevic case that I think is still pending before Your Honour. Other than that, I see no other pending motions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. That's -- that's true.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And I am to say the Trial Chamber will deal with that as expeditiously as possible. On Rule 68, mitigating and exculpatory material, what is your report on that?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: It is ongoing, and we have been -- we have had a positive working arrangement with the Defence. We are using the EDS, and at our last -- at our first meeting with the Defence, in order to try to make the system work better, we have invoked the assistance of the technical people on that, and we're going to keep working with the Defence with the intervention of the technical people to make sure that they are able to have the access that they require. The process, of course, is ongoing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Castle, anything to say on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. CASTLE
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have had some difficulties with EDS, and I have to be frank with the Court that we've had some difficulty with that system. However, we're quite satisfied with the efforts being made by the OTP to assist us in attempting to get around those problems, and at this time we're not asking for any assistance or intervention by the Court in that regard, and we're hopeful that we will not have to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I take account of that. I understand that the Defence has invoked Rule 66(B), and a letter has been sent to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Now, expert reports under 94 bis. Ms. Somers, how many expert reports are you preparing?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Of the new group -- and the reason I distinguish, sir, is because this case is composed of other existing cases, and the number that Your Honour had been given earlier includes - and I believe the number was 15 - includes case -- reports from those cases. At the present time, we are looking at two additional ones specific to this case. They have not been undertaken fully. There are efforts and things are begun, but we have not moved substantially along in that direction yet. It is in the process.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But we need to have a time frame. What is your time frame for --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: For indicating who they are or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: If the Chamber will also permit until the next Status Conference, then we'll be able to have hopefully more than just -- we should be -- if the individuals are the persons we are going to engage, then we should at least have some substantial progress toward the actual report. So if that is an acceptable time frame. At least to begin to get things really moving, and again I want to make sure that I have the number that we would require and speak with -- and also let counsel know which persons we're looking at from other cases. I have begun the inquiry into that and that will be one of the things that I would report to the legal officers and to counsel on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Thanks. I turn now to the Yugoslav Rule 92 bis and 89(F). Are you in a position, Ms. Somers, to indicate to what extent you will be utilising these procedures?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: We would like to do that. The Prosecution would be in favour of trying to in order to streamline any future trial. The Defence has raised certain matters which I believe, when Your Honour gives the Defence the floor, it will inform you of, but we are hopeful that certainly because of the nature of this case being composed of so many other existing cases it would certainly be a useful and efficient mechanism. Of course, whether or not cross-examination is going to be invoked also makes -- will have a bearing on the overall trial time, but the tool itself we will try to use to the maximum extent feasible given the nature of witnesses, depending on what the issues go to, if they fall appropriately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But you have no estimate at this stage of the extent to which you'll be using it?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Not without agreement of the Defence. We'd like to try to have a -- without having to go through motions necessarily. That may end up being the case, but if we can try to agree on certain witnesses and then those that there may be some disagreement on, maybe we may need the intervention, but at this point we haven't been able to sit down on it yet, again because of the state at which the disclosure and the case is at. If the Chamber would like a report, a periodic report as we have the next conference, I can do that, or I can do it at intervals before the next Status Conference, as the Chamber sees helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. It just seems to me that too many things are being put off to the next Status Conference. I think I will require a report within a month.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: On the ...?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: On the use that you'll be making of these procedures under 92 bis and 89(F). Mr. Castle?

utterances.speaker: MR. CASTLE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. On behalf of the Defence, we believe that 89(F) and 92 bis will be used extensively in this case. The difficulty at this point is deciding which particular facts will be admitted pursuant to either one of these two rules. Unfortunately, we're in a situation where the cart is a little bit in front of the horse for us, and our situation is that many of the facts which we believe will be admitted under these two Rules are facts which are derived from these related cases, and the disclosure concerning these related cases has not yet made it to our offices. And based on our investigation of the case, I don't believe there's going to be substantial opposition to the use of these two Rules with regards to crime based evidence, the crime based evidence in the three locations, as I don't see this case to be focused on those factual issues but, rather, the command responsibility and linkage issues. But I have to do my job first as counsel for Mr. Perisic and look into these crime based facts before I can make any final decision on an agreement. I've made it quite clear, I believe, in all of our informal discussions, in our Rule 65 ter Conferences, and I believe perhaps in the Status Conferences this is our attitude towards the use of these two rules, that we do think it is wise and judicious use of the Court's time to invoke these two Rules for a number of facts, that we are in a position right now in the life of this case that it is difficult to pinpoint the facts with certainty that we will be willing to agree upon. Ms. Somers reflected to the Court that we have a document that has been exchanged which is a list of -- of agreed upon facts that we've been exchanging, and we've agreed to sit down in extensive meetings and to go over those facts one by one and perhaps actually even divide up those facts to try to streamline this case. That's what I can report at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, I come now to adjudicated or agreed facts, but we have been discussing that to some extent. But would you just tell me precisely where you are with this, Ms. Somers. I understand the Defence, they have produced a list, a chart listing the facts that they might agree to or might not agree to?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, what the Defence has done is, in response to the list that was sent out by the Prosecution, there are maybe comments which are helpful that may be partially no. So we have an indication of where there are complete differences and then where there are some points of agreement, which is why I think that the approach that Mr. Castle and I have discussed about sitting down as to what aspect of a particular fact could be agreed to will certainly be of assistance. If it saves even 15 minutes of trial time, it will be helpful. But the document is out, we have a response, and we are now -- I know that because counsel is not based here we will have to do a lot either through electronic or with his local assistants, but the process is -- has been -- has begun. I also want to inform the Chamber that I have only been appointed recently to this case and so ask for a bit of -- I apologise if there is less than the complete ability to give you the total history. I've tried to read into it as quickly as possible. We have two new members. We are making it our business to make sure we're familiar with --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It is occurring to me that this is a matter in respect of which a report would be appropriate, so I'm going to require that a report be submitted on this question within two months.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Of the adjudicated --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Within two months.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Of the adjudicated facts?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Would the Chamber allow it to be a preliminary report, because as more information is disclosed, clearly it will be an ongoing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, it will be the first report.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: At the last Status Conference I had indicated that I would be setting a schedule for the filing of pre-trial briefs, but in view of the discussions that have taken place today, I will not do so. I have set dates for -- for two reports, and when those reports are submitted, I'll study them and determine what the next step should be. In the meantime, the next Status Conference must be convened on or before the 15th of June, and I'm going to set Wednesday, the 14th of June, as the date for that Status Conference. Is there any other matter? Mr. Castle?

utterances.speaker: MR. CASTLE
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Somers?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: It can be done, I think, through your legal officers. Counsel and I were discussing one motion -- one order that came out from the Chamber and we need clarification about exactly what the Chamber intends for the breadth of disclosure. I didn't think it was terribly clear in the order, so if we need -- if we need, we will just speak with your legal officer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: This is an order that the Trial Chamber has made?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. And I can do that, but I wanted to let you know that we'll raise it and ask for clarification. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. There being no other matters, the hearing is adjourned.
